findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State how marklas's mistune dependency is satisfied under the stdlib-only engine contract (vendor mistune too, or lazy-import marklas behind a fallback), and reconcile against pyproject.toml `dependencies` + test_core_optionality.py before committing.
evidence: Plan: 'marklas 0.8.6 (pure-Python, mistune-based, MIT ...), vendored under src/rebar/_vendor/marklas/'
pyproject.toml:62-66 core dependencies = pyyaml, jsonschema, referencing only
pyproject.toml:69 'stdlib-only and ship as package data under rebar/_engine/'
adf.py:3 docstring 'Standalone module with no external dependencies (stdlib only)'
resolve_symbol: 'marklas' and 'mistune' both UNRESOLVED — cannot probe the vendored import graph; Partially-verified
Absence: plan Scope lists only marklas + pyproject sha; no mention of mistune vendoring, bundling, or dependency declaration
findings.finding: marklas is described as 'mistune-based', but the plan vendors only src/rebar/_vendor/marklas/ and never states how the transitive mistune dependency is satisfied — while the reconciler engine that imports adf.py is a hard stdlib-only, dependency-free package (pyproject.toml keeps `dependencies` at pyyaml/jsonschema/referencing only; the _engine tree ships as stdlib-only subprocess package data). If vendored marklas imports mistune at runtime, importing adf.markdown_to_adf raises ImportError in a plain install, and the stdlib-only contract enforced by test_core_optionality.py / the family-boundary tests is broken.
findings.location: Engine: vendored marklas section / Scope (src/rebar/_vendor/marklas/) / adf.py
scenarios: A plain `pip install nava-rebar` (no extras) runs a Cloud reconcile that reaches adf.markdown_to_adf and raises ModuleNotFoundError: mistune
test_core_optionality.py-style import sweep sees a new module-scope third-party import in the engine tree
findings.suggested_fix: Vendor mistune alongside marklas under src/rebar/_vendor/ (recording its sha/LICENSE in the same provenance test), OR lazy-import marklas inside the three functions and route conversion errors to the plain-text fallback so `import adf` stays stdlib-clean; add an AC that a no-extras install imports adf.py without ModuleNotFoundError.

Absence: plan never names the import statement adf.py uses to reach the vendored code or how _vendor is packaged into the engine's subprocess sys.path
findings.finding: The vendored engine is placed at src/rebar/_vendor/marklas/, but the reconciler that imports adf.py runs as a subprocess-isolated, stdlib-only package under rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/. The plan does not establish that this out-of-tree _vendor path is importable from the reconciler subprocess's sys.path, nor how adf.py resolves the import (rebar._vendor.marklas vs a relative path).
scenarios: The reconciler subprocess (running from the _engine package data) cannot resolve `rebar._vendor.marklas` because _vendor is not on its path
Wheel packaging omits src/rebar/_vendor from the shipped artifact

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile defect #2 against marklas's documented 'lossless / HTML-comment-annotation' behavior and the plain=True flag — pin exactly which mode is used and why input HTML comments are nonetheless dropped.
evidence: Upstream README (github.com/byExist/marklas, retrieved): 'Lossless bidirectional converter' and 'ADF-only features (panels, mentions, colored text, etc.) are preserved as HTML comment annotations — invisible in rendered Markdown, but fully restorable.'
PyPI (retrieved): 'Pass plain=True to strip roundtrip metadata' — implying marklas normally EMITS HTML-comment metadata rather than dropping it.
The plan asserts the opposite: 'marklas removes HTML comments ... a lone marker becomes the empty string' and makes echo-marker survival an AC.
findings.finding: The plan's defect #2 ('marklas removes HTML comments') contradicts upstream marklas's documented capability, which claims ADF-only features are preserved as restorable HTML comment annotations and that the converter is 'lossless' — the contradiction is unresolved.
findings.location: Section 'Two real defects', item 2 (HTML comments dropped)
scenarios: marklas may only strip HTML comments under plain=True (LLM mode) or may distinguish its own annotation comments from arbitrary input comments — meaning the defect as framed may be mis-scoped or fixable via a flag rather than a custom encode workaround.
The reconciler-echo-marker preservation AC may pass or fail depending on which marklas mode/flag is used, which the plan does not pin.
findings.suggested_fix: State the exact marklas call/flags used (e.g. whether plain=True is set) and clarify whether the drop affects arbitrary input comments vs. marklas's own annotation comments, so the echo-marker-preservation mechanism and AC rest on verified behavior.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Justify choosing/vendoring marklas over established alternatives (md2adf, md-to-adf, @markdown-confluence/lib, wrtnlabs/markdown-to-adf) — note especially that md2adf advertises correct nested-inline-mark handling relevant to defect #1's canonicalizer.
evidence: Web-retrieved prior art: md2adf (pypi.org/project/md2adf, github.com/localghost/md2adf, MIT, mistune-AST-based) which explicitly claims '**bold _and italic_ text** produces three text nodes with the right combination of marks'; md-to-adf (b-yond-infinite-network); @markdown-confluence/lib (markdown-confluence.com); wrtnlabs/markdown-to-adf.
md2adf's advertised correct nested-inline-mark handling is directly relevant to the plan's own defect #1 (the combined strong+strikethrough 2-cycle the plan must hand-fix with a canonicalizer).
The plan states marklas is 'VERIFIED in this worktree' but nowhere compares it against alternatives or explains why marklas is preferred.
findings.finding: The plan commits to vendoring marklas without considering any of the several established Markdown↔ADF libraries that already exist, and gives no anti-repackaging / Rule-of-Three justification for the choice.
scenarios: An alternative library already canonicalizes nested inline marks, obviating the hand-written mark-order canonicalizer the plan commits to building.
Vendoring + sha-pinning + provenance-test overhead is incurred for a library that a maintained alternative could replace.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a short 'Alternatives considered' subsection comparing marklas against md2adf/md-to-adf on the two decisive axes (nested inline-mark correctness vs. the 2-cycle, and HTML-comment/echo-marker preservation), and state why marklas wins despite requiring a hand-written canonicalizer.
